lessons.title: CSS Home
lessons.overview: An overview of the CSS learning path.
lessons.content:
CSS Tutorial

CSS controls how a page looks: spacing, color, layout, and visual hierarchy.

You use CSS to turn a plain HTML page into a polished user interface.
codeExplanations:
• The h1 selector targets all <h1> elements, applying a teal color and larger font size.
  • The p selector targets all <p> elements, setting line height for readability and a dark gray color.

lessons.title: CSS Introduction
lessons.overview: What CSS is and how it connects to HTML.
lessons.content:
CSS Introduction

CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.

It describes how HTML elements should be displayed on screen, on paper, or in other media.
codeExplanations: • The body selector targets the entire page container, setting the default font and background color.

quizzes.question: What does CSS stand for?
quizzes.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.

lessons.title: CSS Syntax
lessons.overview: How CSS rules are written and organized.
lessons.content:
CSS Syntax

A CSS rule set contains a selector and a declaration block with property-value pairs.

Selectors target the elements you want to style, and declarations define the visual result.
codeExplanations: • The h1 selector targets all <h1> elements, applying a blue color and bottom margin.

modules.title: CSS Layout and Responsiveness
modules.description: Modern layout systems and responsive design techniques.

lessons.title: CSS Selectors
lessons.overview: Selectors target elements by tag, class, id, state, or relationship.
lessons.content:
CSS Selectors

Selectors let you apply styles to specific HTML elements, classes, IDs, and pseudo-classes.
codeExplanations:
• The .card selector targets all elements with the class 'card', applying a rounded border.
  • The #hero selector targets the element with the ID 'hero', setting padding.
  • The nav a:hover selector targets anchor tags within a nav element when hovered, adding an underline.

lessons.title: CSS Box Model
lessons.overview: How content, padding, border, and margin work together.
lessons.content:
CSS Box Model

Every element is content plus padding, border, and margin.

Understanding the box model is essential for predictable spacing and layout.
codeExplanations: • The .box selector targets all elements with the class 'box', applying margin, padding, and a border.

lessons.title: CSS Layout
lessons.overview: Layout tools such as display, gap, alignment, and positioning shape the page structure.
lessons.content:
CSS Layout

Modern CSS gives you flexbox, grid, and positioning tools for building responsive interfaces.
codeExplanations: • The .layout selector targets all elements with the class 'layout', setting a grid display with specific column widths and gaps.

lessons.title: CSS Responsive Design
lessons.overview: Responsive CSS adapts the UI to smaller screens using media queries and fluid sizing.
lessons.content:
CSS Responsive Design

Responsive CSS helps a layout adapt to phones, tablets, and desktop screens.
codeExplanations:
• The @media rule applies styles only when the viewport width is 768px or less.
  • The .layout selector targets all elements with the class 'layout', changing the grid column layout to a single column on smaller screens.
